q: Energy is the ability to do ____.
e: Energy is the ability to do work. Work is what this statement is using.

q: Energy exists in many forms and can be converted from one form to ____.
e: Energy exists in many forms and can be converted from one form to another. Another is what this statement is using.

q: Energy sources can be classified as two major sources: conventional sources and ____ sources.
e: Energy sources can be classified as two major sources: conventional sources and non-conventional sources. Non-conventional is what this statement is using.

q: Conventional energy sources are ____ and non-conventional energy sources are renewable energy sources.
e: Conventional energy sources are non-renewable and non-conventional energy sources are renewable energy sources. Non-renewable is what this statement is using.

q: Renewable energy sources are ____ energy sources.
e: Renewable energy sources are sustainable energy sources. Sustainable is what this statement is using.

q: A renewable energy source is generated from unlimited natural sources (e.g. sun, wind, hydropower) and is always replenished and is ____ to the environment.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. A renewable energy source is generated from unlimited natural sources (e.g. sun, wind, hydropower) and is always replenished and is safe to the environment.

q: The most popular renewable energy sources currently are solar energy, wind energy, hydro energy, tidal energy, geothermal energy and ____ energy.
e: The most popular renewable energy sources currently are solar energy, wind energy, hydro energy, tidal energy, geothermal energy and biomass energy. Biomass is what this statement is using.

q: Sun is the primary source of ____.
e: Sun is the primary source of energy. Energy is what this statement is using.

q: Sunlight is a clean, renewable source of ____.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. Sunlight is a clean, renewable source of energy.

q: With the help of photovoltaic technology, solar energy can be used to generate ____.
e: With the help of photovoltaic technology, solar energy can be used to generate electricity. Electricity is what this statement is using.

q: Wind is the natural movement of ____ across the land or sea.
e: Wind is the natural movement of air across the land or sea. Air is what this statement is using.

q: The wind when used to turn the blades of a turbine turns the shaft to which they are attached. This movement of shaft of the generator produces ____.
e: The wind when used to turn the blades of a turbine turns the shaft to which they are attached. This movement of shaft of the generator produces electricity. Electricity is what this statement is using.

q: Hydro energy uses flowing water to power machinery and generate ____.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. Hydro energy uses flowing water to power machinery and generate electricity.

q: Tidal energy is another form of hydro energy that uses tidal currents twice-daily to drive turbine ____.
e: Tidal energy is another form of hydro energy that uses tidal currents twice-daily to drive turbine generators. Generators is what this statement is using.

q: Geothermal energy is more readily available in areas affected by ____.
e: Geothermal energy is more readily available in areas affected by volcanism. Volcanism is what this statement is using.

q: Biomass is plant or animal material used as fuel to produce electricity or ____.
e: Biomass is plant or animal material used as fuel to produce electricity or heat. Heat is what this statement is using.

q: Biomass can also be converted into other forms of energy such as methane gas, ethanol and ____.
e: Biomass can also be converted into other forms of energy such as methane gas, ethanol and biodiesel. Biodiesel is what this statement is using.

q: The four major roles of a renewable energy are (i) electricity generation, (ii) air and water heating/cooling, (iii) reduction of greenhouse gases (GHG), and (iv) replacement of ____ fuels.
e: Heat is energy flowing because of a temperature difference. SI unit is the joule. The four major roles of a renewable energy are (i) electricity generation, (ii) air and water heating/cooling, (iii) reduction of greenhouse gases (GHG), and (iv) replacement of fossil fuels.

q: Non-renewable energy comes from sources that will run out or will not be replenished for thousands or even ____ of years.
e: Non-renewable energy comes from sources that will run out or will not be replenished for thousands or even millions of years. Millions is what this statement is using.

q: Four main types of non-renewable energy sources are oil, natural gas, coal and ____ energy.
e: Four main types of non-renewable energy sources are oil, natural gas, coal and nuclear energy. Nuclear is what this statement is using.

q: Oil, natural gas and coal are collectively called ____ fuels.
e: Oil, natural gas and coal are collectively called fossil fuels. The name used here is fossil.

q: Fossil fuels were formed within the earth from dead plants and animals over ____ of years.
e: Fossil fuels were formed within the earth from dead plants and animals over millions of years. Millions is what this statement is using.

q: Nuclear energy is produced by using elements like uranium and thorium, which cannot be ____.
e: Nuclear energy is produced by using elements like uranium and thorium, which cannot be replenished. Replenished is what this statement is using.

q: Nuclear energy can be used to generate electricity by means of nuclear ____.
e: Nuclear energy can be used to generate electricity by means of nuclear fission. Fission is what this statement is using.

q: In a nuclear reactor, the nuclear fuel is used to carry out sustained fission chain reaction to produce electricity at a ____ rate.
e: In a nuclear reactor, the nuclear fuel is used to carry out sustained fission chain reaction to produce electricity at a controlled rate. Controlled is what this statement is using.
